    wc_bool use_combining;	/* use combining characters */
    wc_bool use_language_tag;	/* use language_tags */
    wc_bool ucs_conv;		/* charset conversion using Unicode */
    wc_bool pre_conv;		/* previously charset conversion */
    wc_bool fix_width_conv;	/* not allowed conversion between different
				   width charsets */
    wc_bool use_gb12345_map;	/* use GB 12345 Unicode map instead of
				   GB 2312 Unicode map */
    wc_bool use_jisx0201;	/* use JIS X 0201 Roman instead of US_ASCII */

    wc_bool strict_iso2022;	/* strict ISO 2022 */
    wc_bool gb18030_as_ucs;	/* treat 4 bytes char. of GB18030 as Unicode */
    wc_bool no_replace;		/* don't output replace character */
    wc_bool use_wide;		/* use wide characters */
    wc_bool east_asian_width;	/* East Asian Ambiguous characters are wide */
} wc_option;

functions.name: Strnew
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty GC-managed string object (Str). Intended as the canonical constructor before appending/copying content.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller should treat the returned Str as a heap-allocated object managed by this library (intended for use with Boehm GC).
The returned value should be checked for NULL if the implementation reports allocation failures that way (unknown).

functions.name: Strnew_size
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new GC-managed string object with at least the specified initial capacity.
requirements: The size argument should be non-negative (inferred).
Very large sizes may be rejected; the library defines STR_SIZE_MAX (INT_MAX/32) as an upper bound used in append macros (capacity growth may abide by similar limits).
Caller should check the return for NULL on allocation failure (unknown).

functions.name: Strnew_charp
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new string object initialized from a NUL-terminated C string.
requirements: The input const char* must point to a valid NUL-terminated string.
Behavior is undefined if the pointer is NULL (unknown).

functions.name: Strnew_charp_n
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new string object initialized from the first n bytes of the given C buffer.
requirements: The input pointer must be valid for reading at least n bytes; it need not be NUL-terminated.
n should be non-negative.
If n is larger than the actual buffer, behavior is undefined (caller responsibility).

functions.name: Strnew_m_charp
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new string composed by concatenating multiple C strings from a variadic argument list. Typically used to build a Str from several const char* pieces.
requirements: The first argument must be a valid const char* string.
The contract for terminating the variadic list is not specified in this header (unknown). Common patterns use a NULL sentinel; verify in implementation.
All provided pointers must point to valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: Strdup
functions.description: Duplicates the given Str, returning a new GC-managed string object with the same contents.
requirements: The input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Returned Str should be treated as independent of the source.

functions.name: Strclear
functions.description: Clears the contents of a Str, typically setting its length to 0 (and keeping capacity).
requirements: The input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: Strfree
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a Str. In a Boehm GC context, this may be a no-op or free auxiliary buffers; callers should still use it when they are done with the object if the API requires.
requirements: The input Str must be non-NULL and previously initialized/allocated by this library.
Do not use the Str after calling Strfree.

functions.name: Strcopy
functions.description: Copies the contents of the second Str into the first, replacing the destination’s contents.
requirements: Both source and destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Destination may be the same as source (unknown).
Destination capacity will be grown as needed (implementation detail; Strgrow exists).

functions.name: Strcopy_charp
functions.description: Copies a NUL-terminated C string into the destination Str, replacing its contents.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Source pointer must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: Strcopy_charp_n
functions.description: Copies the first n bytes from a C buffer into the destination Str, replacing its contents.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Source pointer must be valid for reading at least n bytes.
n should be non-negative.

functions.name: Strcat_charp_n
functions.description: Appends the first n bytes from a C buffer to the end of the destination Str.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Source pointer must be valid for reading at least n bytes.
n should be non-negative.
Total resulting length should not exceed STR_SIZE_MAX (the library’s macro guards appends accordingly).

functions.name: Strcat
functions.description: Appends the contents of the second Str to the end of the first Str.
requirements: Both Str arguments must be non-NULL and initialized.
Total resulting length should not exceed STR_SIZE_MAX (inferred from library macros).

functions.name: Strcat_charp
functions.description: Appends a NUL-terminated C string to the end of the destination Str.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Source must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Total resulting length should not exceed STR_SIZE_MAX (inferred).

functions.name: Strcat_m_charp
functions.description: Appends multiple C strings (variadic list) to the destination Str in sequence.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Each variadic argument should be a const char* to a valid NUL-terminated string.
Termination convention for the variadic list is not specified in this header (unknown); common practice is a NULL sentinel—verify in implementation.
Total resulting length should not exceed STR_SIZE_MAX (inferred).

functions.name: Strsubstr
functions.description: Creates and returns a new Str that is a substring of the input, starting at a given index with a given length.
requirements: Source Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
start index should be in the range [0, source->length] (inferred).
length should be non-negative and not exceed the available characters from start (inferred).

functions.name: Strinsert_char
functions.description: Inserts a single character into the destination Str at the given index, shifting subsequent characters to the right.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Index should be within [0, dest->length] (inferred).
Resulting length should not exceed STR_SIZE_MAX (inferred).

functions.name: Strinsert_charp
functions.description: Inserts a NUL-terminated C string into the destination Str at the given index.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Index should be within [0, dest->length] (inferred).
Source must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Resulting length should not exceed STR_SIZE_MAX (inferred).

functions.name: Strdelete
functions.description: Deletes a span of characters from the destination Str starting at the given index and of the given length.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Index should be within [0, dest->length] (inferred).
Length should be non-negative and the range [index, index+length) should not exceed current length (inferred).

functions.name: Strtruncate
functions.description: Truncates the destination Str to the specified length.
requirements: Destination Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
New length should be in [0, dest->length] (inferred).

functions.name: Strlower
functions.description: Converts all alphabetic characters in the Str to lowercase, in place.
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: Strupper
functions.description: Converts all alphabetic characters in the Str to uppercase, in place.
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: Strchop
functions.description: Removes a trailing character from the Str. Common implementations remove a trailing newline if present; exact semantics are not documented here (unknown).
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: Strshrink
functions.description: Shrinks the string by removing characters from its end. The exact behavior is inferred from naming; Strshrinkfirst is defined as deleting from the front, suggesting this removes from the tail.
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Argument should be non-negative and not exceed current length (inferred).

functions.name: Strshrinkfirst
functions.description: Shrinks the string by removing the first n characters. The macro in this header maps Strshrinkfirst(s,n) to Strdelete(s,0,n).
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
n should be non-negative and not exceed current length (inferred).

functions.name: Strremovefirstspaces
functions.description: Removes leading whitespace (spaces) from the Str, in place.
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: Strremovetrailingspaces
functions.description: Removes trailing whitespace (spaces) from the Str, in place.
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: Stralign_left
functions.description: Returns a new Str that left-aligns the input within a field of the given width, typically padding with spaces on the right. Exact padding character and clipping behavior are not documented (unknown).
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Width should be non-negative (inferred).

functions.name: Stralign_right
functions.description: Returns a new Str that right-aligns the input within a field of the given width, typically padding with spaces on the left. Exact padding and clipping behavior are not documented (unknown).
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Width should be non-negative (inferred).

functions.name: Stralign_center
functions.description: Returns a new Str that centers the input within a field of the given width, typically padding with spaces on both sides. Exact padding distribution and clipping behavior are not documented (unknown).
requirements: Input Str must be non-NULL and initialized.
Width should be non-negative (inferred).

functions.name: Sprintf
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-style formatting and returns it as a new Str. Similar to sprintf but returns a GC-managed Str.
requirements: fmt must be a valid non-NULL format string.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.
Behavior on formatting errors or allocation failures is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: Strfgets
functions.description: Reads a single line from the given FILE* and returns it as a new Str. Likely stops at newline or EOF (unknown exact inclusion of newline).
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open stream for reading.
May return NULL on EOF or error (unknown); caller should be prepared to handle NULL (inferred).

functions.name: Strfgetall
functions.description: Reads the entire contents of the given FILE* and returns it as a new Str.
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open stream for reading.
Behavior on I/O error is not specified (unknown).
Large files may exceed STR_SIZE_MAX (inferred limit).

functions.name: Strgrow
functions.description: Ensures the Str has additional capacity for growth. Used internally (e.g., via macros) to expand the buffer when appending.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and initialized.
Typically called when length+1 >= area_size or approaching STR_SIZE_MAX (inferred).

functions.name: wc_is_combining
functions.description: Returns whether the given wide character value is a combining character (e.g., a diacritic or mark that combines with a preceding base character). Typical usage is to test characters during text processing (rendering, normalization, or segmentation) to handle combining marks specially. Documentation is not present in this header; behavior is inferred from the name and context in a character set/Unicode-related header.
requirements: cc must be a valid, initialized wc_wchar_t value representing a single character in the library’s internal wide-character encoding (likely Unicode); exact encoding details are unknown.
The caller should interpret the return as boolean (true if combining, false otherwise); precise mapping to integer values for wc_bool is unknown.
Behavior for invalid or out-of-range code points is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: wc_get_ucs_table

requirements: ccs must be a valid character set identifier (wc_ccs) recognized by the library
The returned wc_table* (if non-NULL) should be treated as read-only and passed back to related APIs that accept wc_table*

functions.name: wc_ucs_to_any

requirements: cc must be a valid wc_wchar_t produced by this library’s conversion routines
Returned value is a Unicode code point; behavior for invalid cc is unknown

functions.name: wc_any_to_any
functions.description: Converts an internal wide character from one encoding domain to another using the provided conversion table.
requirements: t must be a non-NULL, valid conversion table compatible with the source representation of cc
cc must be a valid wc_wchar_t value produced by this library
Result for unmappable input is unspecified; caller should handle potential replacement or error values

functions.name: wc_ucs_to_any_list
functions.description: Converts a Unicode code point to an internal wide character using one of several possible conversion tables supplied in a list.
requirements: tlist must be a valid pointer to a list/array of wc_table* entries; exact list termination convention is unknown
Each element of tlist must be a valid wc_table* as returned by wc_get_ucs_table
ucs should be a valid Unicode scalar (<= 0x10FFFF, excluding surrogates)
Selection criteria among tables is not documented; callers should expect the first table that can map ucs to be used

functions.description: Converts an internal wide character to another representation, honoring CES (character encoding scheme/state) tracked in st.
requirements: st must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized wc_status encoding/conversion state object; exact initialization requirements are unknown
cc must be a valid wc_wchar_t value produced by this library
Caller should handle possible stateful output; behavior for invalid state is unspecified

requirements: st must be non-NULL and initialized for ISO-2022 processing; structure and initialization details are unknown
cc must be a valid wc_wchar_t from this library
Caller should be prepared for stateful output, including escape sequences represented in wc_wchar_t form

functions.description: Converts a Unicode code point to an internal representation corresponding to ISO-2022 output.
requirements: ucs should be a valid Unicode scalar value (0x0000..0x10FFFF, excluding surrogates)

functions.name: wc_ucs_to_iso2022w
functions.description: Converts a Unicode code point to an internal wide representation appropriate for ISO-2022 (wide) processing.
requirements: ucs should be a valid Unicode scalar value (exclude surrogate range)

requirements: ucs should be a valid Unicode scalar value (exclude surrogate range)

functions.name: wc_ucs_to_utf8
functions.description: Convert a single UCS/Unicode code point (ucs) to its UTF-8 byte sequence and write the bytes to utf8. Returns the number of bytes written. Typical usage: prepare a buffer, call once per code point, then append or process the produced bytes. Notes: This implementation appears to support up to 6-byte UTF-8 forms (non-standard extensions) in addition to standard UTF-8 (up to 4 bytes). It likely does not append a NUL terminator.
requirements: utf8 must point to writable memory large enough to hold the longest possible UTF-8 sequence produced by this implementation; given the constants (WC_C_UTF8_L2..L6), allocate at least 6 bytes.
ucs should be a valid code point for the intended character repertoire; behavior for out-of-range or invalid values is unspecified in this header.
The function likely does not NUL-terminate the output; the caller must manage string termination if needed.
The function converts exactly one code point; the caller should handle iteration over input text and buffer management.

functions.name: wc_utf8_to_ucs
functions.description: Decode a UTF-8 sequence starting at utf8 into a single UCS/Unicode code point and return it. Intended to be called at a position pointing to the first byte of a UTF-8 sequence. Notes: The header does not specify error handling or how many bytes are consumed; the function likely reads as many continuation bytes as implied by the first byte. Behavior on invalid sequences is unknown.
requirements: utf8 must point to a buffer containing at least one complete UTF-8 encoded character starting at utf8; ensure sufficient accessible bytes for the maximum sequence length (up to 6 bytes in this implementation).
utf8 must be aligned to the start of a UTF-8 sequence (i.e., not a continuation byte).

The caller must track/advance the input pointer by the number of bytes consumed; this function’s signature provides no out-parameter for length consumed, so consumption length handling is unspecified here.
Behavior for malformed sequences is unspecified; callers should not pass invalid UTF-8.

functions.name: wc_conv_from_utf8
functions.signature: extern Str wc_conv_from_utf8(Str is, wc_ces ces);

import random
import struct
import itertools

# We generate NUL-terminated C strings intended to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# in the provided fuzzer stubs. The goal is to exercise different code paths:
# - Plain ASCII
# - UTF-8 with multibyte sequences
# - Strings resembling charset/locale names (for wc_* guess/convert APIs)
# - Mixed lengths including empty string
# - Strings with embedded NUL not allowed for C strings -> we avoid embedded NUL
# - Variations in size but keep under ~2KB as stubs cap sizes
# The returned bytes buffer may be used by the harness to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"hello", b"world", b"test", b"Str", b"append", b"insert", b"truncate",
    b"upper", b"lower", b"spaces", b"align", b"center", b"left", b"right",
    b"utf8", b"utf7", b"unicode", b"iso2022", b"hangul", b"jis", b"gbk",
]

# Common charset and locale-like tokens to trigger wc_* guess/convert paths
CHARSET_NAMES = [
    b"UTF-8", b"utf8", b"UTF-7", b"Shift_JIS", b"SJIS", b"EUC-JP", b"ISO-2022-JP",
    b"ISO-8859-1", b"latin1", b"cp1252", b"GBK", b"GB18030", b"Big5", b"KOI8-R",
    b"US-ASCII", b"ASCII", b"JIS_X_0208", b"JIS_X_0213", b"HZ-GB-2312",
]
LOCALE_NAMES = [
    b"en_US", b"en_US.UTF-8", b"ja_JP.SJIS", b"ja_JP.EUC-JP", b"zh_CN.GB18030",
    b"zh_TW.Big5", b"ko_KR.EUC-KR", b"ru_RU.KOI8-R", b"de_DE.ISO-8859-1",
    b"C", b"POSIX",
]

# Some multibyte UTF-8 sequences: emoji, CJK, combining marks
UTF8_UNITS = [
    # Simple BMP
    "é".encode("utf-8"),  # U+00E9
    "Ω".encode("utf-8"),  # U+03A9
    "漢".encode("utf-8"),  # U+6F22
    "한".encode("utf-8"),  # Hangul U+D55C
    "あ".encode("utf-8"),  # Hiragana U+3042
    # Combining mark sequence: a + combining acute
    "a\u0301".encode("utf-8"),
    # Emoji (4-byte)
    "😀".encode("utf-8"),  # U+1F600
    "🧪".encode("utf-8"),  # U+1F9EA
]

# Utility to build a NUL-terminated C string without embedded NULs

def make_c_string(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    payload = payload.replace(b"\x00", b"")
    return payload + b"\x00"


def build_ascii(rand: random.Random) -> bytes:
    n = rand.randint(0, 10)
    parts = [rand.choice(ASCII_WORDS) for _ in range(n)]
    sep = rand.choice([b" ", b"-", b"_", b"", b", "])
    data = sep.join(parts)
    return make_c_string(data)


def build_charset_like(rand: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix charset names and locale names
    if rand.random() < 0.5:
        token = rand.choice(CHARSET_NAMES)
    else:
        token = rand.choice(LOCALE_NAMES)
    # Optionally add variants like lowercase/uppercase or prefixes/suffixes
    mods = []
    if rand.random() < 0.3:
        mods.append(b" ")
        mods.append(rand.choice([b"//TRANSLIT", b"//IGNORE", b";q=0.8"]))
    if rand.random() < 0.2:
        token = token.lower()
    if rand.random() < 0.2:
        token = token.upper()
    data = token + b"".join(mods)
    return make_c_string(data)


def build_utf8_text(rand: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a mixed UTF-8 string, ensure well-formed
    parts = []
    length = rand.randint(1, 64)
    for _ in range(length):
        pick = rand.random()
        if pick < 0.5:
            # ASCII letter/digit/punct excluding NUL
            ch = rand.choice([ord(' ')] + list(range(0x21, 0x7f)))
            parts.append(bytes([ch]))
        else:
            parts.append(rand.choice(UTF8_UNITS))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    # Bound length to ~1500 to satisfy append limits comfortably
    if len(data) > 1500:
        data = data[:1500]
    return make_c_string(data)


def build_format_string(rand: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Provide printf-like formats used by Sprintf stub
    formats = [b"%s", b"%d %u", b"hex:%x str:%s num:%ld", b"%08x-%s", b"%ld"]
    fmt = rand.choice(formats)
    return make_c_string(fmt)


def build_small(rand: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Very small strings, including empty
    size = rand.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8])
    if size == 0:
        return b"\x00"
    data = bytes([rand.randint(1, 255) for _ in range(size)])  # avoid NUL
    return make_c_string(data)


def build_long_ascii(rand: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a longer but bounded ASCII string to exercise growth paths
    target = rand.randint(50, 800)
    chunk = rand.choice([b"A", b"abc", b"-", b" "])
    data = (chunk * (target // max(1, len(chunk)) + 1))[:target]
    return make_c_string(data)


BUILDERS = [
    build_small,
    build_ascii,
    build_charset_like,
    build_utf8_text,
    build_format_string,
    build_long_ascii,
]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """Generate a seeded bytes buffer containing a NUL-terminated C string.
    The buffer targets APIs that consume const char* via FUZZ_PARAM_STR in stubs.
    Size is kept <= 4096 bytes.
    """
    rand = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose 1-3 strings and concatenate them with separators to feed multi-arg stubs too
    k = rand.randint(1, 3)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(k):
        builder = rand.choice(BUILDERS)
        parts.append(builder(rand)[:-1])  # drop the trailing NUL to concatenate safely
    sep = rand.choice([b" ", b",", b";", b"|", b"\n", b"//", b"::", b" "])
    payload = sep.join(parts)
    # Ensure final size constraint
    if len(payload) > 4095:
        payload = payload[:4095]
    return make_c_string(payload)

from typing import List

# Generator for an arbitrary byte buffer tailored to the provided fuzz stubs.
# Goals per stub usage:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): Return diverse NUL-terminated-friendly or raw byte payloads that
#   exercise text processing, charset detection, substring, copy/append behaviors.
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): Return a plausible temporary path-like string. The harness
#   will create and open it; we only need to provide a name-like buffer.
# The fuzzer harness wraps our bytes into a std::string. We therefore embed multiple
# alternatively-interesting payloads and choose deterministically by seed.
# Constraints:
# - Produce <= 4096 bytes.
# - Valid inputs (no intentionally malformed structures beyond arbitrary bytes).

# Helper: Various interesting corpus building blocks
ASCII_PRINTABLE = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
WHITESPACE = b" \t\r\n\f\v"
PUNCT = b"!@#$%^&*()_+-={}[]|:;\"'<>?,./`~"

# Common UTF-8 sequences covering 1..4 bytes
UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    "ASCII simple text\n".encode(),
    "Caféâñ – en dash & emoji ".encode("utf-8", errors="strict") + "😊".encode("utf-8"),
    "日本語かな漢字".encode("utf-8"),
    "한글 Hangul 테스트".encode("utf-8"),
    "Русский текст".encode("utf-8"),
]

# UTF-7 valid snippets (for wc_conv_from_utf7 users elsewhere). Not strictly needed
# here but useful for charset auto-detection diversity.
UTF7_SNIPPETS = [
    b"Hello+ACE-World+ACE-",           # "Hello!World!"
    b"+ZeVnLIqe-",                    # "日本"
    b"+APw-UTF7+AD0-OK",              # "~UTF7=OK"
]

# Bytes with NULs and control characters to test n-limited copy/append and unknown push
CTRL_BLOCK = bytes(range(0x00, 0x20)) + b"\x7f"

# Some likely-file names for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
FILENAME_CANDIDATES = [
    b"/tmp/wtf_test.bin",
    b"/tmp/wtf_out.txt",
    b"/tmp/.hidden_wtf",
    b"/tmp/wtf-\xf0\x9f\x98\x8a.bin",  # emoji in UTF-8
    b"/tmp/wtf-data-123456",
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))


def _build_filename(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Pick from candidates or assemble a safe temp-like path
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(FILENAME_CANDIDATES)
    # Construct: /tmp/prefix-<rand>.bin
    suffix = ''.join(rng.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789') for _ in range(8)).encode()
    return b"/tmp/wtf-" + suffix + b".dat"


def _build_texty(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose a text-like buffer mixing ASCII, whitespace, punctuation, and UTF-8
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Start with an UTF-8 snippet
    parts.append(rng.choice(UTF8_SNIPPETS))
    # Add ASCII word soup
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        wlen = rng.randint(3, 12)
        word = bytes(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(wlen))
        parts.append(word)
        parts.append(rng.choice([b" ", b"\n", b"\t"]))
    # Add punctuation run
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        plen = rng.randint(5, 20)
        parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(PUNCT) for _ in range(plen)))
    # Maybe add UTF-7 snippet to aid auto-detect variety
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(rng.choice(UTF7_SNIPPETS))
    data = b''.join(parts)
    # Trim to cap
    return data[:1024]


def _build_binary(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Include NULs, controls, and random payload; good for n-based ops and unknown push
    chunks = []
    # lead-in controls
    chunks.append(CTRL_BLOCK[: rng.randint(4, len(CTRL_BLOCK))])
    # random chunk with occasional NULs
    rlen = rng.randint(16, 256)
    rb = bytearray(rlen)
    for i in range(rlen):
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            rb[i] = 0
        else:
            rb[i] = rng.randrange(1, 256)
    chunks.append(bytes(rb))
    # tail signature
    chunks.append(b"\x00END")
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    return data[:1024]


def _build_repeated_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Patterns that exercise width, Hangul checks, and substring boundaries
    patterns = [
        "A" * 64,
        "가나다라" * 16,            # Hangul
        "━━★☆" * 32,               # wide line/box chars
        "abc123\n" * 64,
    ]
    pat = rng.choice(patterns).encode("utf-8")
    # Pre/append spaces to engage trimming functions
    pad_left = b" " * rng.randint(0, 8)
    pad_right = b" " * rng.randint(0, 8)
    return (pad_left + pat + pad_right)[:1024]


def _mix_buffers(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix multiple constructed parts to form a rich buffer
    parts = []
    for builder in ( _build_texty, _build_binary, _build_repeated_pattern ):
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            parts.append(builder(rng))
    # Insert explicit NUL between segments sometimes, to affect n slicing
    if parts and rng.random() < 0.5:
        sep = b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 3)
        data = sep.join(parts)
    else:
        data = b"".join(parts)
    return data[:2048]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide intent: filename-like or data buffer. The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME()
    # and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() independently. We return a buffer used for both; when used as
    # filename, std::string will accept UTF-8 and ASCII paths, so ensure path-like option
    # available frequently.
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.2:
        data = _build_filename(rng)
    elif mode < 0.5:
        data = _build_texty(rng)
    elif mode < 0.8:
        data = _build_binary(rng)
    else:
        data = _mix_buffers(rng)

    # Ensure non-empty to satisfy places expecting at least one byte; but also sometimes
    # empty is a valid and interesting case (handled by stubs). Keep small probability empty.
    if not data and rng.random() < 0.2:
        return b""
    if not data:
        data = b"0"  # minimal non-empty

    # Final cap at 4096
    return data[:4096]

import random
from typing import List

# Data type: file bytes (arbitrary)
# Generate interesting, valid file contents for Strfgets/Strfgetall and as a byte buffer for wc_putc.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"Hello",
    b"World",
    b"Test",
    b"WTF-ENC",
    b"ASCII",
    b"Line",
    b"Data",
    b"Sample",
    b"Quick",
    b"Brown",
    b"Fox",
    b"Pack",
]

UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    "😀",
    "漢",
    "€",
    "¡",
    "ß",
    "Ω",
    "한",
    "あ",
    "日",
    "✓",
]

BINARY_CHUNKS = [
    bytes([0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]),
    bytes([0xFF, 0xFE, 0xFD, 0xFC]),
    bytes([0x7F, 0x00, 0x41, 0x42, 0x43]),
    b"\x00END\x00",
]

LINE_ENDINGS = [b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\r"]

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    s = rng.choice(UTF8_SNIPPETS)
    return s.encode('utf-8')

def _rand_ascii_word(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)

def _make_line(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.45:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii_word(rng))
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                parts.append(b" ")
        elif choice < 0.85:
            parts.append(_rand_utf8(rng))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                parts.append(b" ")
        else:
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                parts.append(rng.choice(BINARY_CHUNKS))
            else:
                parts.append(str(rng.randint(0, 9999)).encode('ascii'))
                if rng.random() < 0.2:
                    parts.append(b" ")
    line = b"".join(parts)
    if len(line) > target_len:
        line = line[:target_len]
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and len(line) > 4:
        pos = rng.randint(1, len(line)-2)
        line = line[:pos] + b"\x00" + line[pos:]
    return line

def _make_long_block(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    lower = max(64, max_len // 8)
    upper = max_len
    if lower > upper:
        lower = max(1, min(upper, 64))
    target = rng.randint(lower, upper) if upper >= 1 else 1
    line = _make_line(rng, target)
    return line

def _compose_file(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = budget

    # Optional BOM
    if remaining >= 2 and rng.random() < 0.3:
        bom = rng.choice([b"\xEF\xBB\xBF", b"\xFF\xFE", b"\xFE\xFF"]) if remaining >= 3 else b"\xFF\xFE"
        bom = bom[:remaining]
        chunks.append(bom)
        remaining -= len(bom)

    # Lines
    num_lines = rng.randint(3, 12)
    for i in range(num_lines):
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        # choose a target length but not exceeding remaining-1 (reserve for newline if any)
        max_line = max(0, remaining - 1)
        if max_line == 0:
            target_len = 0
        else:
            target_len = rng.choice([
                rng.randint(0, min(8, max_line)),
                rng.randint(0, min(40, max_line)),
                rng.randint(0, min(120, max_line)),
            ])
        line = _make_line(rng, target_len)
        # newline selection
        if i == num_lines - 1 and rng.random() < 0.5:
            le = b""
        else:
            le = rng.choice(LINE_ENDINGS)
        chunk = line + le
        if len(chunk) > remaining:
            chunk = chunk[:remaining]
        chunks.append(chunk)
        remaining -= len(chunk)
        if remaining <= 0:
            break

    # Long block without newline
    if remaining > 64 and rng.random() < 0.8:
        block_budget = rng.randint(128, min(1024, remaining)) if remaining >= 128 else min(remaining, 64)
        long_block = _make_long_block(rng, block_budget)
        long_block = long_block[:block_budget]
        chunks.append(long_block)
        remaining -= len(long_block)

    # Repeated pattern
    if remaining > 0 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        pat = (b"ABC" + _rand_utf8(rng) + b"123")
        if len(pat) == 0:
            reps = 0
        else:
            max_reps = max(1, remaining // max(1, len(pat)))
            reps = rng.randint(1, min(max_reps, 10)) if max_reps >= 1 else 1
        rep_chunk = pat * reps
        rep_chunk = rep_chunk[:remaining]
        chunks.append(rep_chunk)
        remaining -= len(rep_chunk)

    # Trailing binary tail
    if remaining > 0 and rng.random() < 0.6:
        upper = min(64, remaining)
        lower = 1 if upper >= 1 else 0
        tail_len = rng.randint(lower, upper) if upper >= 1 else 0
        tail = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(tail_len))
        chunks.append(tail)
        remaining -= tail_len

    return b"".join(chunks)[:budget]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    budget = rng.choice([
        rng.randint(1, 64),
        rng.randint(65, 256),
        rng.randint(257, 1024),
        rng.randint(1025, 2048),
        rng.randint(2049, 4096)
    ])
    buf = _compose_file(rng, budget)

    if not buf:
        buf = b"\n"

    # Ensure first byte non-NUL for wc_putc pointer use
    if buf[0:1] == b"\x00":
        buf = b"A" + buf[1:]

    return buf[:4096]
